answer: Sybil resistance comes from a bond per identity that cannot be diluted: each agent locks collateral at a bridge contract, and a slow unbonding river keeps that capital exposed after a fault is found. Creating N fake personas needs N separate stakes, so the marginal cost of each extra voice never falls toward zero as with free sign-ups. If graders link two identities to one operator, every bond in the cluster is slashed, so a raven who splits a fixed budget across many keys only multiplies the ways to lose it. Reward is capped per controller, so scale brings liability, not profit.
